title: Convening of Anti-profiteering Task Force in Light of Water Price Increases
what_it_is: Convening of Anti-profiteering Task Force in Light of Water Price Increases

sections.label: Utilities share of business costs
sections.summary: Utilities cost accounts for less than 1% of business costs on average for most services industries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Utilities cost, which includes water and electricity costs, accounts for a relatively small share of business costs for firms in the services sector, at less than 1%, on average, for most services industries.

sections.label: No profiteering committee needed
sections.summary: MTI does not see the need to set up a committee to look into profiteering, as feedback can go through channels like REACH.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: They can also do so through Government feedback channels, such as the feedback unit Reaching Everyone for Active Citizenry @ Home (REACH).

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Hence, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) does not see the need to set up a committee to look into profiteering at this point.

sections.label: SPRING Capability Development Grant
sections.summary: SPRING's Capability Development Grant defrays up to 70% of qualifying project costs for SMEs building capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In particular, SPRING's Capability Development Grant (CDG) provides support for SMEs in building capabilities to grow their businesses by defraying up to 70% of the qualifying project costs.

sections.label: Coffee chains not raising prices
sections.summary: Several coffee chains, including Toast Box and Ya Kun Toast, said they would not raise prices in the near term.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For example, in an article published in TODAY newspaper on 23 February 2017, in response to the increase in water prices, several coffee chains here, including Toast Box and Ya Kun Toast, have said that they would not increase their prices in the near term.

sections.label: No broad-based business cost impact
sections.summary: CASE's hotline, website and mobile apps will receive feedback, and the cost increase is not expected to exceed 1% or 2%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And if it so happens then, then I think this is where CASE's hotline, website and mobile apps will be available for feedback to be received.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: It affects business segments more than others, and even in the retail services sector, as I have said earlier, the cost increase is not expected to be more than 1% or 2%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, we do not expect a broad-based impact on the actual costs of businesses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We will continue to keep a watchful eye on how this will impact, say, after the price goes up in July.

sections.label: CASE monitoring coffee shop prices
sections.summary: CASE will monitor coffee shop drink prices and publicise coffee shops that have not raised their prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: From CASE's point of view, we will continue to monitor prices of drinks in coffee shops and in the event that one coffee shop raises its price more than others, we will be happy to publicise coffee shops which have not raised the price of their coffee and other drinks.

sections.label: Feedback diverted to CASE
sections.summary: The speaker asks why feedback is diverted to CASE instead of MTI investigating, and whether CASE has enough manpower and resources for the added caseload.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I just want to ask why exactly are we diverting the feedback towards CASE, which is a non-Government organisation, instead of MTI taking the feedback and investigating; and, secondly, whether MTI feels that CASE has sufficient manpower and resources to take up the additional caseload now.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But CASE, as an organisation that helps to educate consumers, plays an important role here in helping consumers to understand their purchasing power as consumers and to be able to exercise that.
